mechanism_narrative: A low level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds regardless of the current economic cycle.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% (as measured at t-1mo).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.2 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which precedes corporate earnings slowdowns and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.2 percentage points over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 1% in the past month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending manufacturing slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% over the past month.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS is above its 1-year moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% annually signals accelerating inflation, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payrolls (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market weakness (e.g., job losses in a growing workforce), predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS grows by less than 0.1% and UNRATE rises by more than 0.1 percentage points in the past month.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle recoveries, a rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening manufacturing, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In early-cycle recoveries, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO increases by more than 0.5% over the past month.
